pois.name: Shore Temple
pois.summary: Twin granite towers on the surf line, and the Pallava leap from carving rock to building with dressed stone. Its tiered vimanas are the direct ancestors of every later South Indian temple tower.
history: Unlike everything else here it was built, not carved — dressed blocks raised into place under Narasimhavarman II Rajasimha. Three shrines share the compound: two to Shiva facing opposite ways, and between them an earlier shrine holding a reclining Vishnu cut from the bedrock the temple was built around.

Twelve centuries of salt wind have rounded the carving almost smooth. The ASI planted the casuarina windbreak behind it for that reason, and the 2004 tsunami briefly drew the sea back far enough to expose more masonry along the shore.

pois.name: Pancha Rathas
pois.summary: Five free-standing temples, each carved downward out of a single boulder — a sculptor's catalogue of roof forms running from thatched hut to multi-storeyed vimana. None was ever consecrated.
history: They are named for the Pandava brothers and Draupadi, but the names are late and have nothing to do with what the shrines were for. What they really are is a set of experiments: five different roof types tried side by side in stone, working out forms that had until then been built in brick and timber.
All five are unfinished. Because the sculptors worked top-down, the upper storeys are complete while the bases are still rough — which is exactly why they show how the work was done.

pois.name: Descent of the Ganges
pois.summary: A whale-backed cliff nearly 30 m long, worked into a crowded relief of gods, sages, and life-size elephants around a natural cleft that once ran with water. Also read as Arjuna's Penance.
history: The natural fissure down the middle is the point of the whole composition: water was channelled down it so the carved river would actually run. Nagas swim up the cleft; everything else on the rock turns to face it.

Which story it tells is still argued. Either Bhagiratha's penance brings the Ganges down to earth, or Arjuna fasts to win a weapon from Shiva. A famous detail below the elephants settles nothing but says a lot: a cat stands on one leg imitating the ascetic, while mice gather trustingly at its feet.

pois.name: Krishna's Butterball
pois.summary: A six-metre granite boulder resting on a bare slope at an angle that looks impossible. Not carved, but part of the site's identity and a fixture of every visit.
history: It is a natural erosion remnant, not a placed stone, and it sits on a short contact patch on sloping rock. Its back is sheared flat, which only shows from behind.

pois.name: Varaha Cave Temple
pois.summary: A small excavated mandapa whose panels include Vishnu as the boar lifting the earth, and Gajalakshmi bathed by elephants — among the finest Pallava figure carving anywhere.
history: Four large panels, one to a wall. Varaha the boar raises the earth goddess clear of the ocean; Trivikrama strides across the world; Gajalakshmi sits while elephants pour water over her; Durga stands attended. The pillars rest on seated lions, a Pallava signature.

sources.text: Wikipedia, “Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram” § Varaha (CC BY-SA)

pois.name: Mahishasuramardini Mandapa
pois.summary: Two facing panels stage opposites: Durga charging the buffalo demon on one wall, Vishnu asleep on the serpent Ananta on the other. Movement and stillness, cut side by side.
history: The Durga panel is the most kinetic carving on the site — she rides her lion into the demon's ranks with her attendants pressing forward, while Mahishasura gives ground. Directly opposite, Vishnu lies utterly still on the coils of Ananta. Putting the two on facing walls looks deliberate.

pois.name: Olakkanneshwara Temple
pois.summary: On the hilltop above the Mahishasuramardini cave, roofless now and once used as a lighthouse. The best vantage point over the whole site and the coastline.
history: Built on the boulder directly above the Mahishasuramardini cave. It lost its tower long ago and served as a lighthouse into the colonial period before the present tower was put up beside it. The climb is short but almost entirely unshaded.

ticket.note: No ticket recorded for this monument.
